newsitem.title: JAPAN: GM to market Saturn in Japan next April.
newsitem.headline: GM to market Saturn in Japan next April.

text.p: Saturn Japan, a division of General Motors Japan Ltd, said on Wednesday that it will start selling cars at 14 outlets in Japan next April. The firm is the Japanese unit of General Motors Corp.

Saturn Japan also said it has signed retailer agreements with three companies -- Nissan Prince Shiga Hanbai Ltd, Shiga Kotsu KK and Kobe Isuzu Motors Ltd -- bringing the total number of Saturn retailers to nine.
Nissan Prince is a local independent dealer for Nissan cars. Kobe Isuzu is 16.9 percent owned by Isuzu Motors Ltd. GM owns 37.4 percent of Isuzu.
Saturn Japan will have a total of 20 outlets by the end of 1997. It will unveil the right-hand-drive car at the Osaka Import Automobile Show, which opens on November 22.
"We have studied the Japanese market carefully and our product was developed to meet the needs of this market," Donald Hudler, president of GM unit Saturn Corp, said in a statement.
Saturn will introduce three models into Japan, the SL2 sedan, the SW2 wagon and the SC2 coupe.
Saturn's plant in Spring Hill, Tennessee, will start production of those models next January.
